title: De lineis curvis non in eodem plano sitis, quae maximi minimive proprietate sunt praeditae

deep.reconstruction:
Page 33 of E740 finishes Problem IV and states Problem V.

Problem IV. In the earlier steps, the extremal curve in space was shown to lie in the plane z = ny + ax. With p = dy/dx and u = y/x, a first integral was found by adding two arctangents and taking the tangent of the sum: pu − β = f(p + u + 2α), where α = an/(1+n²), β = (1+a²)/(1+n²) and f is an integration constant.

Section 30 integrates this algebraically.
1. Solving for p gives p = (β + f(u+2α))/(u − f). The printed letter for β looks like an ε-shaped glyph.
2. Hence p − u = (β + 2αf + 2fu − u²)/(u − f).
3. The homogeneous substitution y = ux gives dx/x = du/(p−u) = (u−f)du/(β + 2αf + 2fu − u²).
4. The numerator is −½ times the derivative of the denominator. So ln x = C − ½ ln(β + 2αf + 2fu − u²), i.e. x√(β + 2αf + 2fu − u²) = g, with g a new constant.
5. Putting u = y/x gives (β + 2αf)x² + 2fxy − y² = g².

So the projection on the xy-plane is a central conic centred at the origin. Substituting y = (z − ax)/n gives the xz-projection, also a conic. Since the curve is planar, it is itself a conic, i.e. a plane section of a quadric cone/cylinder. Euler remarks that a seemingly very hard problem has reduced to a very simple solution.

Problem V is then stated: with v = √(x²+y²+z²) and w = w(v) arbitrary, find the space curve making ∫ w(v) ds an extremum. This is the ray path in a spherically symmetric isotropic medium, equivalently a geodesic of a conformally flat radially symmetric metric. It is equivalent, via Maupertuis/Jacobi, to motion under a central force. Its solution (next pages) gives the Euler–Lagrange equations in the form (y dx − x dy)/v² = w dp/(w′ v s²), etc. These lead to planarity of the orbit through the centre.
errors: Sign misprint in the final conic: from x²(β+2αf+2fu−u²) = g² with u = y/x one gets βx² + 2αf x² + 2f xy − y² = g², i.e. +2fxy. The print has −2fxy. The conclusion (a conic) is unaffected.

Notational clash: the integration constant written g is distinct from the ε/β-like glyph standing for β. The machine transcription conflates them, and also writes a for α in 'g+f(u+2a)' and '2af'. The letter a (from z = ny + ax) and α = an/(1+n²) are different quantities.

ideas.what: Integration of a first-order ODE homogeneous in x,y by the substitution y = ux, then separation of variables
ideas.where_published: Institutiones calculi integralis I (E342) and many papers

ideas.what: Extremal space curve of Problem IV is planar and its projections are central conics, so the curve is a conic
ideas.modern_name: explicit solution of an Euler–Lagrange system for a space curve
ideas.where_published: E740 itself (Mémoires de l'Acad. St-Pétersbourg IV, 1813)

ideas.what: Problem V: extremize ∫ w(r) ds for space curves with radially symmetric weight
ideas.modern_name: rays in a spherically symmetric medium / geodesics of conformally flat radial metric / Jacobi–Maupertuis central-force orbits
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Methodus inveniendi 1744, planar case; Maupertuis principle); Jacobi metric 1837

deep.surprise_reason: Routine integration completing a worked example. The only noteworthy item is a sign misprint (−2fxy should be +2fxy). Problem V is a classical problem Euler had already treated in the plane.
transcription_corrections: In 'p = (g+f(u+2a))/(u−f)', the image shows an ε/β-like glyph (standing for β), not g, and α (alpha), not a: p = (β + f(u+2α))/(u−f).
Likewise 'g+2af+2fu−uu' should read β(ε-glyph) + 2αf + 2fu − uu throughout. Only the right-hand constant in x√(...) = g is the letter g.
The final equation in the image reads 'εxx + 2αfxx − 2fxy − yy = gg', with ε (β) and α. Mathematically the middle term should be +2fxy.
